name: bulirsch_stoer
title: Bulirsch-Stoer Algorithm
description: High-accuracy ODE values from Richardson extrapolation of the modified midpoint rule on each grid interval.
case: y' = -y, y(0) = 1, on five points from 0 to 0.5. The check vector is that solution matrix, column by column.
args: Increasing grid where the solution is returned.
Tolerance for Richardson extrapolation on each step.

name: midpoint
title: Bulirsch-Stoer Algorithm
description: Implicit midpoint rule on an equispaced grid. A scalar stage is solved with fzero, and a system with Broyden.
usage: midpoint(f, t0, tfinal, y0, tol = 1e-08, kmax = 101, ...)
args: Initial value, a row or column vector.
Present in the signature; the implicit grid does not use it.

name: ode23s
title: Non-stiff (and stiff) ODE solvers
description: Modified Rosenbrock pair of orders 2 and 3. A missing Jacobian is a centered difference with step 5e-6.
usage: ode23s(f, t0, tfinal, y0, jac = NULL, ..., rtol = 1e-03, atol = 1e-06, hmax = 0.0)
case: y' = -y, y(0) = 1, on [0, 0.4]. The check vector is the solution column.
args: Initial value, a vector or one column.
Jacobian jac(t, y). NULL uses finite differences.
Maximum step. 0 uses a tenth of the interval.

name: ode45
title: Non-stiff (and stiff) ODE solvers
description: Dormand-Prince (4,5) pair. The step advances with the fifth-order estimate, and one state is returned as a vector.
usage: ode45(f, t0, tfinal, y0, ..., atol = 1e-6, hmax = 0.0)
args: Initial value, a vector or one column.

name: ode78
title: Non-stiff (and stiff) ODE solvers
description: Fehlberg (7,8) pair. Thirteen derivative evaluations per attempt, and the step advances with the eighth-order estimate.
usage: ode78(f, t0, tfinal, y0, ..., atol = 1e-6, hmax = 0.0)
case: y' = -y, y(0) = 1, on [0, 0.4]. The check vector is the solution column.
args: Initial value, a vector or one column.

name: ode23
title: Non-stiff (and stiff) ODE solvers
description: Bogacki-Shampine Runge-Kutta pair of orders 2 and 3 with an adaptive step.
usage: ode23(f, t0, tfinal, y0, ..., rtol = 1e-3, atol = 1e-6)
case: y' = -y, y(0) = 1, on [0, 0.4]. The check vector is the solution column.
args: Initial value, a vector or one column.

name: rkf54
title: Runge-Kutta-Fehlberg
description: Runge-Kutta-Fehlberg pair of orders 5 and 4. The fifth-order value is kept, and the fourth-order difference sets the next step.
usage: rkf54(f, a, b, y0, tol = .Machine$double.eps^0.5, control = list(), ...)
args: Tolerance used to accept a step and to grow it.
Optional hmin, hmax, and jmax. A unique prefix is accepted.

name: deeve
title: Event Detection in ODE solution
description: Times at which one solution component equals a level, by linear interpolation. A level outside the sampled range is missing.
case: On eleven points of exp(-x) from 0 to 1, the time where the solution equals exp(-0.25).
args: Abscissae of a stored solution, sorted and increasing.
Solution values, one row per abscissa.
1-based column. NULL uses the last column, and only the first index is kept.

name: deval
title: Evaluate ODE Solution
description: Linear interpolation of a stored ODE solution. Abscissae outside the grid stay missing.
case: exp(-x) on eleven points from 0 to 1, interpolated at 0.25, 0.55, and 0.83.
args: Abscissae of a stored solution, sorted and increasing.
Solution values, one row per abscissa.
Abscissae where the solution is wanted.
1-based columns to return. NULL returns every column.

name: rk4
title: Classical Runge-Kutta
description: Fixed-step classical Runge-Kutta of order 4 for one equation.

name: rk4sys
title: Classical Runge-Kutta
description: Fixed-step classical Runge-Kutta of order 4 for a first-order system. Each row of y is one time.
case: y1' = -y1 and y2' = -2 y2 from (1, 2), four steps on [0, 0.5]. The check vector is the solution, column by column.
args: Derivative of the system, f(x, y).
Initial value, one entry per equation.

name: bvp
title: Boundary Value Problems
description: Finite-difference solution of y'' = f(x) y' + g(x) y + h(x), with the boundary values stored at the ends of the grid.
usage: bvp(f, g, h, x, y, n = 50)
case: y'' = y on [0, 1], y(0) = 1, y(1) = exp(-1), with eight interior points.
args: Coefficient of y', or a constant.
Coefficient of y, or a constant.
The two ends of the interval.
Number of interior grid points, an integer of at least 2.

name: cranknic
title: Crank-Nicolson Method
description: Average of a forward Euler slope and a backward Euler slope. The implicit stage is a scalar root when the state has length one.
args: Initial value, a row or column vector.

name: newmark
title: Newmark Method
description: Implicit Newmark step for one second-order equation. The state holds the value and its first derivative, and each stage is a Broyden root.
usage: newmark(f, t0, t1, y0, ..., N = 100, zeta = 0.25, theta = 0.5)
case: y'' = -y, y(0) = 1, y'(0) = 0, eight points on [0, 0.5]. The check vector is the solution, column by column.
args: Second derivative y'' = f(t, y), with y of length 2.
Number of grid points, an integer greater than 1.

name: abm3pc
title: Adams-Bashford-Moulton
description: Third-order Adams-Bashforth predictor and Adams-Moulton corrector. The third starting slope is evaluated at the second node.

name: euler_heun
title: Euler-Heun ODE Solver
description: Explicit Euler step. When improved is true, that prediction is replaced by the trapezoidal Heun average.
usage: euler_heun(f, a, b, y0, n = 100, improved = TRUE, ...)
case: y' = -y, y(0) = 1, eight Heun steps on [0, 0.5].
args: Derivative y' = f(t, y), returning one value.
TRUE uses the Heun correction. FALSE keeps Euler.

name: shooting
title: Shooting Method
description: Secant search on the initial slope of a second-order equation so the end condition is zero. Each trial is integrated with ode45.
usage: shooting(f, t0, tfinal, y0, h, a, b, itermax = 20, tol = 1e-6, hmax = 0)
case: y'' = -y, y(0) = 1, y(0.5) = cos(0.5), with slope guesses 0 and -1. The check vector is the solution, column by column.
r: c(shooting(function(t, y1, y2) -y1, 0, 0.5, 1, function(u, v) u - cos(0.5), 0, -1, tol=1e-6, hmax=0.1)$y)
py: np.ravel(shooting(lambda t, y1, y2: -y1, 0, 0.5, 1, lambda u, v: u - math.cos(0.5), 0, -1, tol=1e-6, hmax=0.1)["y"], order="F")
args: Second derivative y'' = f(t, y, y').
Initial value, not the initial slope.
First guess of the initial slope.
Second guess of the initial slope.
Stop when the end condition is this small, and pass it to ode45.
Maximum ode45 step. 0 uses that solver's default.
